# tools-review

The review_threads and review_comment tools: a task's agent reads and answers the threads of its review.

- **Runs in:** the harness process
- **Source:** [lisp/modules/harness-tools-review.el](../../lisp/modules/harness-tools-review.el)
- **Loaded:** when enabled (see `harness-enable-modules`)
- **Requires:** [tools](tools.md), [session](session.md)
- **Required by:** [patch-review](patch-review.md)

## About

A task's review is a set of threads of comments (harness-patch-review.el).
The user writes in them; the task's agent reads and answers them with
two tools.

`review_threads` lists the threads of the agent's own task -- or of
another task, named by id -- with the comments the user sent: the ids
the agent answers by, who wrote what, where in the change it is.  The
feedback that sends a task back already carries the threads it is
about, so the tool is for what the agent has lost since, a compacted
context say.

`review_comment` adds a comment of the agent's to a thread, and may
close the thread or open it again.  The comment records the agent, the
session and this very tool call, so that whoever reads the thread can
follow it to the point of the conversation it came from, and the
commit the agent was at, so that a reply that says "fixed" says where.
With no thread it starts one, on the change as a whole, or on a file
and line of it.

Both are offered to task sessions: a session that is no task's has no
review (the filter `agent/tools` removes them), unless it names a task.

## Provides

### Tools

- `review_comment` — Answer a thread of the review of your work, or start one. The thread id is given in the feedback after "[thread ...]", and review_threads lists them. Write what you did or why you disagree, briefly, in Markdown: the review draws it rendered, so name code in `backquotes`, put lines of code in a fenced block and steps in a list. Close the thread (status closed) once what it raises is done; leave it open when it is not, or when you want the user`s answer, and never close a thread you only argued against. Without thread a new thread starts: on the change as a whole, or on file and line of it, to explain something to the user where they will read the diff. The comment records this call, so the user can follow it back to this point of the conversation. With thread and status but no body, only the status changes.
- `review_threads` — List the threads of comments in the review of your task's work: for each, its id, whether it is open or closed, where in the change it is, and the comments the user sent, with who wrote them. Use it to find the thread to answer with review_comment when the feedback that sent the task back is no longer in your context. With status, only the open or only the closed threads; with task, another task's review.
